correctness.rationale: Facet potentials have saturated cycle differences: balanced ±1 increments in even order and one zero with remaining balanced signs in odd order; saturation rank proves these are precisely facets. Choosing a spanning path gives alternating integer parity classes of sizes ceil(n/2) and floor(n/2). Their centered squared sum is at least ab/n, with equality only at adjacent two-level potentials: exactly 2 even or 2n odd facets. Uniform balanced signed increments converge, as linearly interpolated bridge, to Brownian bridge; centering the sum gives continuous-map limit Q=∫(B-∫B)^2. Circular Fourier decomposition gives Q=Σ_{k>=1}(Zk1²+Zk2²)/(4π²k²), Laplace sqrt(s/2)/sinh sqrt(s/2), moments 1/12 and 1/360. Nearest-plane bound is only coarse contextual estimate. Boundary n=3 and both parities checked.
